svg.title: Proposition 27: Partition-Lattice Transport Under Node Aggregation
svg.desc: What this figure shows: Repository theorem. Proposition 27 formalizes when a partition of fine physical nodes has a mathematically well-defined counterpart after several fine nodes are represented by one coarse node.. Visible guideposts include: Which fine partitions still have an exact meaning when several physical nodes become one coarse node?; NODE AGGREGATION; Surjective node map; a : Vf ↠ Vc; Fc = a⁻¹(c); Each coarse node represents one fine aggregation fiber.. How to read it: follow the diagram in the direction of its arrows and use each box, panel, inequality, or highlighted region only with the meaning printed beside it. Main takeaway: this is the visual companion to Proposition 27; the proposition document supplies the assumptions, proof, and exact scope of every implication. Scientific status: Proposition 27 theorem/certificate visual. It is not independent empirical evidence and does not, by itself, identify a physical or latent variable with consciousness.
svg.text: P27 - Partition-Lattice Transport Under Node Aggregation
Which fine partitions still have an exact meaning when several physical nodes become one coarse node?
Each coarse node represents one fine aggregation fiber.
A coarse node cannot belong to two partition blocks.
Lift and descent are inverse on their declared domains.
Coarse partitions are exactly the aggregation-saturated fine partitions
Refinement order, meet, and join are preserved by the lift/descent correspondence.
Each coarse state uses one fiber
Node reduction and state compression are distinct operations.
A lossless block state may retain all fine states inside a fiber.
Valid aggregation can preserve or erase dependence, not create it.
no saturation ⇒ no coarse partition semantics
saturation + lossy state map ⇒ κc may be smaller than κf
Semantic obstruction and observational attenuation are mathematically different and must not be conflated.
P27 transports partitions through node aggregation. Intervention aggregation, full P11 equivalence, physical completeness, and experience remain open.
